## Context / Problem

At the audited snapshot, `src/rebar/llm/config.py` was 799 lines and `LLMConfig.from_env` occupied lines 566-768. ADR 0056 and closed ticket `candied-senseless-squirrel` anticipated this next headroom breach.

## Approach

Keep `LLMConfig.from_env` as the sole precedence and composition facade. Extract cohesive table-driven readers for model/provider, budgets, tracing, web, and path settings into focused sibling modules. Preserve current precedence, validation, defaults, and patch-visible exports during this extraction; the separately ADR-gated internal-shim work may later migrate private compatibility paths.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/config.py`
- focused LLM configuration reader siblings
- `tests/unit/test_config_llm.py` and config precedence/patch tests

Cascade flag: true. Recensus semantic, string, dynamic-import, environment, and monkeypatch references.

## Testing

Use table-driven cases for config-file, environment, explicit override, malformed value, missing value, and cross-field precedence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Model/provider, budget, tracing, web, and path parsing are owned by cohesive readers without duplicating precedence logic.
- [x] `LLMConfig.from_env` remains the only composition/precedence facade.
- [x] Existing defaults, validation failures, environment/config precedence, and patch-visible behavior are byte/value equivalent.
- [x] Focused config tests plus module-size, complexity, lint, and typecheck gates pass.
